claim: A 3-zone bay packs into 2 carry bags under 12 kg in total (team deck)
law: Mass budget from the model at 0.70 kg/m2 (FXP-PLT-001 D1, F5) and PETG at 1.27 g/cm3; 12 kg less two empty bags buys 14.9 m2 of sheet with no hardware (12.4 m of 1.2 m wall)
check: FT1 needs 25.92 m2 of wall, 4.55 m2 of leaves and two tail leaves (sheet 22.3 kg) plus 19.4 kg of clips, feet, pins, pads and prints: 43.1 kg with bags, 3.59 times the claim. The panels alone exceed 12 kg. 4 bags of 12 kg or 3 of 20 kg; a two-zone bay is 34.7 kg. The platform's own zigzag U bay is 14.3 kg (FXP-PLT-001 P17, D15); with moulded cored feet (0.15 kg) and clips (0.04 kg), platform D15 (b), this bay is still about 35.0 kg, so only a higher target in more bags fits it. At 800 g/m2 the sheet would weigh 25.5 kg (independent review 2026-11-12: holds). Changing the pack target changes a user-facing claim

claim: A functional 3-zone bay of about 20 m2 needs 18 P12 duos, 4 flap leaves and 2 tail leaves (12 sheets of 1,220 x 2,440 mm)
law: Plan geometry from the model: two zigzag long walls of 7 duos, four zigzag stubs, four doorways with one leaf each, two corner tails
check: 21.6 m of wall; interior 19.19 m2 on joint lines, about 1 % less clear (zones 1 Intake 5.48, 2 Assessment 5.48, 3 Treatment 8.22 m2)

claim: A 1.2 m wall marks a boundary between cohorts; the plan keeps the 1 m spacing WHO asks for; it is not a privacy screen
law: WHO AFRO triage stations: seats at least 1 m apart, 1 to 2 m between health worker and patient, one-way flow; ANSUR II eye heights (NCSU summary)
check: Zones are 2.34 m wide on joint lines, so the layout gives the spacing. Every standing adult (eye 1,421 to 1,753 mm) sees heads and upper bodies over a 1212 mm wall, but a short observer 0.5 m from it cannot see a patient on a floor stretcher for 2.31 m behind it, or a trolley top for 0.99 m (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, restated). A staff-position rule (stand at a doorway, not at a wall) goes in the procedure; separation is never by airflow (FXP-PLT-001 L1)

claim: Zigzag P12 walls and stubs stand under their own weight, cold and hot
law: Greenhill self-weight buckling of a flat strip (FXP-PLT-001 P2): h_cr = (7.837 EI/q)^(1/3) = 1441 mm; a 600 mm leaf held on both vertical edges by a 30 deg fold or angle clip, orthotropic formula with zero twisting stiffness (FXP-PLT-001 P3); hot = half the 23 C stiffness (FXP-PLT-001 section 10); platform load factor 2
check: As drawn in v0.1 (flat duos, inline joints) a P12 strip had factor 1.73 cold and 0.87 hot, failing hot (FXP-PLT-001 v0.2 agrees, 0.87; platform request 1). Fixed with the platform's v0.2 rule S1: every wall and stub is a zigzag, leaves at 15 deg, folds and angle clips at 30 deg, inline joints only where a tee return meets them (rule S4). A held leaf is 9.43 cold and 4.72 hot; a leaf with one free edge (the wall ends at the entry and exit, the tails) about 4.68 cold and 2.34 hot (A16, an assumed plate coefficient); a flap leaf hung from its lower sleeve 5.05 cold and 2.52 hot. All exceed 2 cold and 1 hot; the free-edge figure rests on an assumed coefficient
closed_by: FXP-PLT-001 rule S1 (F1, v0.2); FXT-DEC-001 F10 (standing instruction); T7 hot soak at TRL 4

claim: A long wall pushed outward with 178 N at the BIFMA height next to a stub joint does not tip
law: Rigid wall piece about the outside outrigger tips, as FXP-PLT-001 P7; push at 1110 mm; unballasted 52.1 N (fails); two 5 kg bags on each stub's anchor foot, which now lifts with the stub (independent review 2026-11-12: refuted as first drawn, the stub lifted out of a plain foot slot); anchor uplift 103 N against 176 N for two through-pegs (FXP-PLT-001 v0.2 P9; v0.1 used 201 N, factor 1.96), factor 1.71; the tee clips carry the stub's 113 N of lift in shear against 351 N, factor 3.12. FXP-PLT-001 P9 now fails with a fix proposed (D14): demand on a clip in a bowing leaf is not bounded on paper
closed_by: FXT-DEC-001 F4 (standing instruction, 2026-10-23); T3 peg uplift, T7 tip test at TRL 4

claim: A push anywhere along a long wall, away from a stub, does not tip the wall
law: A lone zigzag P12 duo on two feet tips at 4.5 N outward and 5.9 N inward (FXP-PLT-001 P6 method, leaves 78 mm outside the joint line); a free wall end at the entry or exit jamb at 8.7 N outward and 8.9 N inward; a zigzag stiffens the wall up its height, not along it, so it still cannot carry a push sideways to the stubs (a 600 mm leaf bows past 25 mm at 5.8 N, FXP-PLT-001 P4)
check: Fails: between stubs the walls tip at about 5 to 15 N against 178 N (independent review 2026-11-12: refuted). Buttresses every 1.2 m would each need about 20 kg of ballast; the honest options are a stated limit (boundaries that tip if leant on, as platform limit L1) with a lower lateral criterion, or a different structure. A scope and safety trade-off
closed_by: Proposed, awaiting Amish: FXT-DEC-001 D7; FXP-PLT-001 D5

claim: A tee joint carries a stub's overturning couple into the long wall in edge bearing
law: Couple 178 N x 1110 mm over the 900 mm between clip heights: 220 N per clip height, borne by the pushed-side wall leaf's edge on the round core of the angle tee over 100 mm and both 0.26 mm skins; at a corner there is no panel beyond the joint, so the couple fell on peg tension (176 N per clip, factor about 1, independent review 2026-11-12: refuted). Fixed: a 600 mm tail leaf outside each end-stub corner makes it a tee (F7). Bearing stress in MPa against half of the PP yield of 24 MPa
check: 4.2 MPa <= 12 MPa
closed_by: FXT-DEC-001 F7 (standing instruction); T3 and T7 at TRL 4

claim: The bay does not slide when bumped with 178 N next to a stub
law: Friction mu W of the pushed piece (40.2 kg with ballast); hard plastic feet mu 0.2 to 0.35, rubber on concrete 0.45 to 0.85 (Engineering ToolBox)
check: Bare PETG feet slide at 79 to 138 N (fails). Fixed with a 2 mm EPDM pad under every foot (F5): 177 to 236 N, so the wet low end only just reaches 178 N; a single duo between stubs slides at a few newtons, as S6 (independent review 2026-11-12: weak). Friction on wet clinical vinyl with hypochlorite to measure
closed_by: FXT-DEC-001 F5 (standing instruction); T7 at TRL 4

claim: Two people with no training deploy a functional 3-zone bay in under 15 minutes (team decision gate)
law: Step count from the model (20 panels, 46 clips, 22 feet, 22 pads, 4 leaves, 8 pins, 10 bags) x ASSUMED action times, two people at 70 to 85 % useful time (A9, A10)
check: As first drawn 16.3 to 47.5 min: fails at both ends. With fix F6 (sleeves and strike holders stay on the leaves, pads bonded under the feet, bags filled before the clock and laid in 10 to 20 s) 12.0 to 34.9 min: the fast end meets 15 min, the slow end does not (independent review 2026-11-12: weak). Error modes (wrong foot type, stub on the wrong wall) not counted. Only the timed trial can close it
closed_by: FXT-DEC-001 F6; decision gate test V1 at TRL 4

claim: One zone goes from flat pack to standing in under 5 minutes (team deck)
law: Two duos, three feet, seven clips, one leaf on two pins and two filled bags at the A9 times
check: 1.6 to 4.7 min including the leaf and ballast (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, now counted); assumed times

claim: The magnetic catch holds a leaf shut against a draught and the leaf opens with no more than 22.2 N
law: N42 disc 12.7 x 3.2 mm: 28.6 N to a thick steel plate at contact (K&J D82); pull scaled with B squared on the disc axis (A13) to a 2.5 mm gap; push plate at 956 mm from the hinge against the catch at 1155 mm; ADA 404.2.9 22.2 N used as the push target (ADA itself excludes catch release)
check: First drawn as two leaves meeting edge to edge, the catch acted in shear and held about 2 N (independent review 2026-11-12: refuted). Fixed (F3): one leaf per doorway, opening downstream only, closing on a stop block upstream with the magnet in pull on a stainless strike: about 12.9 N at the catch, 15.3 N at the push plate, against a draught need of 0.57 to 2.84 N. Thin-strike and gap losses are first order; measured hold to set the cover
closed_by: FXT-DEC-001 F3 (standing instruction); V3 at TRL 4

claim: Each doorway passes a stretcher and a wheelchair
law: Clear width at the floor between the wall jamb's foot and the anchor foot, whose block sits 15 deg off the doorway line; ADA 404.2.3 clear width 815 mm; fabric stretcher 750 mm wide (CQC NATO); 1054 mm at the entry and exit; 971 mm in the upstream approach beside the bags; 1149 mm past the open leaf
closed_by: FXT-CAL-001 section 7; turning space in S32

claim: The bay never narrows the host tent's or room's exits
law: Minnesota State Fire Code tent sheet (MSFC 3103.12): 2 exits of 72 in (1,829 mm) for 10 to 199 occupants; egress paths kept clear and unobstructed
check: A placement rule, not physics (independent review 2026-11-12: weak): the bay needs 8.8 x 2.9 m plus 1.5 m of approach at the entry and exit, so a host tent or hall at least about 12 x 4 m clear of its exit routes; its own doorways are internal and narrower than a tent exit

claim: The bay adds about 1279 MJ of fire load
law: FXP-PLT-001 P23: 27.8 MJ/m2 of FXP-S4FR (PP 39.7 MJ/kg, FSRI); PET gross heat of combustion 21.4 MJ/kg (UQ fire laboratory) for the PETG parts and polyester bags
check: Sheet 887 MJ, PETG clips and feet 288 MJ (not FR rated), bags 105 MJ (independent review 2026-11-12: refuted at 851 MJ, now counted); 1207 MJ of sheet at P18. True, so the FR sheet is mandatory, PETG parts are few and small, and the bay stays 1 m from heaters and flames
closed_by: FXP-PLT-001 rule FR1; FXT-DEC-001 C9 (FR clip grade)

claim: The bought sheet is the platform FR grade (NFPA 701 TM1, at most 700 g/m2)
law: FXP-PLT-001 P24 and F5; the priced listing (cplast.net 48964WFR) says its FR board 'meets most city and state codes' and links a data sheet
check: Grammage and an NFPA 701 TM1 and ASTM E84 report for the bought lot are not on the listing; at 800 g/m2 the sheet mass rises by 1/7 (S1)

claim: Sheet, clips, pads, pins, strikes and the enclosed magnet tolerate 0.5 % hypochlorite and 70 % alcohol wipes
law: FXP-PLT-001 P18 to P20 for PP and PETG; EPDM and stainless not on those charts; chloride pits zinc plating
check: Strikes and washers changed to stainless (A2 is weakly magnetic, so a ferritic grade may be needed, C7); a printed 2 mm cover is not a hermetic seal, so the magnet pocket is sealed with a bonded cap (independent review 2026-11-12: weak); EPDM and the cap to the T4 coupons

claim: Every surface facing a care zone can be wiped
law: FXP-PLT-001 v0.2 rules E1 (cut edges, groove shoulders and ends, holes sealed), E2 (groove face away from care zones, or covered by a flexible clear PP strip) and E3 (clips off for cleaning); the 13.6 mm flat-bottomed groove is on every duo's back face
check: Wall grooves face outside the bay (print faces in), so they meet E2 by layout. The four stubs face a zone on both sides: their groove is covered by a clear PP strip heat-staked or taped along both shoulders (F2, now platform rule E2; platform request 2 resolved). Strip lift under wiping is unproven (independent review 2026-11-12: weak)
closed_by: FXT-DEC-001 F2; FXP-PLT-001 E2; FXP-PLT-001 T6

claim: Hinges, catches, clip slots, pads and feet can be cleaned between uses
law: Clip slots have 0.25 mm clearance a side (4.5 mm slot, FXP-PLT-001 v0.2); pin hinges, stop blocks and foot slots are crevices; pads sit at floor level
check: Cleanable only with the leaves lifted off their pins, clips removed (FXP-PLT-001 rule E3) and pads bonded and edge-sealed (F5); disassembly time counted in turnaround

claim: Colour-coded zones are read the same way by every team
law: START (CHEMM): red immediate, yellow delayed, green minor, black expectant; SALT and the Model Uniform Core Criteria: immediate red, delayed yellow, minimal green, expectant gray, dead black; ISO 3864-1: red prohibition and fire, yellow warning, blue mandatory, green safe condition
check: The deck's 'green zone' and 'red zone' for process steps would read as triage categories and as ISO safe and fire colours (fails as drawn). Fixed (F1): process zones carry a numeral, a word and an arrow on neutral white and black; the way out of the bay is a neutral sign, not an ISO 7010 emergency exit (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, corrected); red, yellow and green appear only as category bands with the category word (FXP-PLT-001 C2, C4)

claim: Zone words can be read from anywhere in their own zone
law: ANSI Z535 ratio (25 ft per inch of letter height), halved for poor light; 60 mm words and 150 mm numerals in a band 1,015 to 1,195 mm above the floor (ADA 703.5.6); distance in m against the largest zone's diagonal (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, restated per zone)

claim: Cues are understood across languages and cultures
law: ISO 7010 aims at safety information that 'relies as little as possible on the use of words'; WHO EMT minimum standards ask for interpreters at triage and respect for cultural aspects such as separation of gender in waiting areas
check: Numerals, arrows and symbols carry most of it; words in the local languages; colour meanings vary by culture: to assess with the field partner
closed_by: FXP-PLT-001 T5 with users at TRL 4

claim: The 3-zone bay fits the deck's 20 m2 of floor
law: Zone areas from the plan; outriggers reach 300 mm outside every wall line; approach at entry and exit
check: Interior 19.19 m2 on joint lines (the zigzag walls shorten the pitch to 1171 mm), a little under 20 m2, and the bay needs 8.8 x 2.9 m (25.87 m2) of clear floor plus about 1.5 m of approach at each end (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, the claim fails as stated). Restating the site requirement is a user-facing change

claim: The prototype bay's parts cost about USD 1174, against the USD 800 value-engineering target
law: Priced BOM (bom/bom.csv), cited prices checked 2026-11-12; printed parts at filament cost
check: USD 1174.23, USD 374.23 over the target (a value-engineering target, not a limit, STANDARDS 18); drivers sheet USD 405 and freight USD 150. A print service at USD 0.10/g would add about USD 1076; 13.4 kg of PETG is about 672 printer-hours at 20 g/h (A11). At the 1,100-sheet price the sheet falls by USD 120; under USD 500 is not shown (independent review 2026-11-12: refuted as 'plausible', restated as a number)

claim: Panels, clips, hinges and catches survive 50 or more deployments
law: FXP-PLT-001 P13, P14 (hinge strain 4.0 %, snap strain 1.4 %); about 200 passages a day per doorway ASSUMED: 2,800 swings in a two-week use, 140,000 in 50 uses
check: Clips and folds as the platform; the leaf's stainless pin in a printed bore and the catch see 150,000 cycles over the life (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, raised)
closed_by: FXP-PLT-001 T2, T3; V3 at 150,000 cycles at TRL 4

claim: The bay is for use indoors or inside a tent
law: FXP-PLT-001 P8 and limit L2 (10 m/s exceeds the ballasted restoring moment)
check: Inherited from the platform; lower walls lower the wind moment but do not change the limit

claim: The bay supports IPC cohorting practice; it makes no claim on airborne or droplet transmission
law: FXP-PLT-001 L1 and STANDARDS 25.5b; WHO AFRO and CDC rely on distance, PPE and ventilation, not partitions
check: Claims limited to physical separation, one-way flow and cues (FXT-CLM-001)

claim: The bay stands on uneven field floors (team risk)
law: Feet seat each panel 12.5 mm above the floor on a 2 mm pad; a duo spans 1.17 m between feet
check: A floor step larger than the pad's give racks the joint; slope and step tolerance are to measure
closed_by: T7 on a 1:50 slope at TRL 4

claim: Ballast bags lie clear of the leaf's swing and the doorway's clear width
law: Leaves open downstream only; bags stacked on the upstream outrigger of each anchor foot (F8); jamb feet keep only their outside outrigger
check: First drawn, a leaf swept 3.5 mm over a bag (independent review 2026-11-12: refuted). Now no bag lies under a swing; bags reach 165 mm into the upstream approach, leaving 971 mm; bags and feet are marked on the floor

claim: Smoke from the FR sheet in a fire is no worse than other FR plastics in a care space
law: FXP-PLT-001 section 2.2 and D11: brominated FR with antimony trioxide; combustion products include hydrogen bromide and antimony oxides
check: To assess with the halogen-free FR question (platform D11)

claim: The bay configures to 2 to 4 zones and each configuration stands next to its stubs
law: Each further zone adds 2 pitches: two wall duos, one stub, one leaf and their hardware; rigid-piece tipping as S5
check: Two-zone about 34.7 kg, four-zone about 48.7 kg; in a two-zone bay each wall carries one stub and tips at 161.4 N with two bags, so it needs 11.3 kg (three bags) at that stub (independent review 2026-11-12: weak)
closed_by: FXT-CAL-001 section 5; configuration rule in PR-006

claim: The bay is not an impact barrier
law: A 150 kg trolley at 1 m/s carries 75 J (ASSUMED case); the energy to tip one wall piece is about 27 J and one duo about 1 J
check: A trolley or a falling person knocks walls over; stated in the claims register and on the zone signs ('boundary, do not lean')

claim: A stretcher can be turned through the serpentine doorways
law: Zone clear width about 2.35 m; a 2.1 m stretcher with a bearer at each end about 2.9 m long (ASSUMED); doorways 1.2 m wide at alternate sides
check: Not shown on paper: the swept path through a 90 deg turn in a 2.35 m zone is tight; a swept-path drawing and a mock-up walk-through decide it

claim: People can leave the bay quickly in an emergency
law: Each zone has two doorways; leaves open downstream with a push of about 16 N (S11) and are pulled the other way; walls are 1.2 m high
check: Forward evacuation passes 1 to 3 leaves; backward needs a pull. Leaves lift off their pins in seconds for a mass move; evacuation drill in V1

claim: The hinge side of a leaf does not trap fingers
law: Leaf and stub edges each sit 6 mm from the pin axis, so the hinge gap opens and closes between about 0 and 12 mm as the leaf swings
check: That range traps fingers as drawn first. Fixed: a flexible EPDM finger guard bonded across the hinge gap on both faces (F9)

claim: Passing a doorway needs no hand contact
law: Leaves open with about 16 N (S11) on a push plate 820 to 1,120 mm from the hinge, 814 to 974 mm above the floor
check: A hip, forearm or trolley can push the plate; returning upstream needs a pull by hand, so the leaf edge is a touch surface cleaned with the high-touch surfaces

claim: Ballast does not bring soil or wet bags onto a clinical floor
law: Site sand or soil can carry spores and dirt; coated polyester sits at floor level
check: Bags filled with clean sand off the clinical floor, closed and wiped; a sealed, wipeable bag or a water bag to source (C8)

claim: Signs and doorways are usable by people with low vision and by wheelchair users
law: ADA 703.5.6: visual characters at least 40 in (1,015 mm) above the floor; 703.5.1 contrast; doorway clear width S12
check: Signs moved to a band 1,015 to 1,195 mm with dark characters on light; leaves carry a dark edge band on white walls; feet and bags marked on the floor; the 43 mm outriggers along every wall line remain a trip edge for low vision

claim: PP sheet and PETG clips keep their stiffness and grip in a hot tent
law: PETG glass transition about 81 C (MakeItFrom); PP stiffness at 50 C ASSUMED half (A15); black clips in sun-heated tents
check: Self-weight factor of S4 falls to about 0.86 for a flat strip; snap tongues and pegs creep under sustained load; maximum use temperature to set
closed_by: Hot soak in T7; FXP-PLT-001 T3 at 40 and 50 C

claim: Folds and clips survive cold use
law: PP turns brittle towards 0 C; folds strain the 0.26 mm skin by 4 %
check: Minimum use temperature to set; fold and clip only when the panels are at room temperature

claim: The sheet tolerates UV inside a tent
law: Interprofile outdoor grade 2,500 h SAE J1960; LaminaCorr Ultra FR lists an anti-UV additive; the priced FR board's UV grade not stated
check: UV grade to confirm with the supplier (C1)

claim: The catch magnet's field falls below the 0.5 mT ACGIH limit for pacemakers close to the stop block
law: On-axis field of a 12.7 x 3.2 mm disc, Br 1.3 T ASSUMED (A13); ACGIH 0.5 mT for implanted cardiac pacemakers (UCSD summary); distance in mm
closed_by: Label on each stop block: 'magnet, keep pacemakers 10 cm away'

claim: A user can tell when a clip is fully home
law: FXP-PLT-001 P9 (v0.2) assumes both through-pegs engaged through both skins; a half-engaged clip looks like a full one
check: A printed witness line 40 mm from each clipped edge disappears into the clip mouth when the clip is home; the peg tips show in the back-wall sockets; a tug test in the build plan

claim: Untrained people assemble it right first time
law: Six foot types, 46 clips, stubs on alternate walls, duos that fold one way, leaves that hang one way
check: Feet colour-keyed and slotted so each fits only its joint; fold direction printed on each duo's back; a pictorial card in each bag; error modes in the FMEA
closed_by: V1 with untrained users at TRL 4

claim: Printed parts can be made in the prototype time
law: 13.4 kg of PETG at 20 g per printer-hour (A11)
check: About 672 printer-hours: weeks on one printer, so a print farm or a makerspace pool for the prototype and moulding at scale
